units.translation: 119 is meaningless in the manuscripts and only apparently healed by Hermann's ⟦1⟧ instead of ⟦2⟧; for then ⟦3⟧ refers to Orestes, and ⟦4⟧ (441) means protector, for which one cites ⟦5⟧ Hik. 1. Correctly Weil ⟦6⟧ (cf. ⟦7⟧ ⟦8⟧).
for they are friends, not resembling my own

121 ⟦1⟧ (or -⟦2⟧) is not necessary, since ⟦3⟧ and -⟦4⟧ occur side by side. The ⟦5⟧’ after ⟦6⟧ is to be adopted without hesitation from f g h (just as it is also to be retained at ⟦7⟧); cf. ⟦8⟧. ⟦9⟧ (⟦10⟧) etc. On the naming of the name see on 116.

⟦1⟧, if 124 ⟦2⟧ is correct M; cf. ⟦3⟧, which according to Reisig is the correct spelling for ⟦4⟧; see on this Ellendt in the Lexicon ⟦5⟧, ⟦6⟧, Rabe, Rh. Mus. XLVII, 413 (⟦7⟧ mostly the Laur. of A. and Soph., likewise Ven. A of the Iliad).

125 ⟦1⟧ is by no means covered by ⟦2⟧ ⟦3⟧; for there ⟦4⟧ is a variant, which Bentley here demanded by conjecture; cf. ⟦5⟧ ⟦6⟧; the corruption here was especially easy through ⟦7⟧; ⟦8⟧ however (cf. 334 ff.) is both closer to the letter-forms and stronger than ⟦9⟧ (Wakefield, ⟦10⟧ 208), cf. Schütz. On ⟦11⟧ cf. 71. –
In any case these things have been done, and he will not escape
For what is fated for Zeus except to rule forever?

⟦1⟧ cf. Homer ⟦2⟧ 2 ⟦3⟧; to be sure, this is not exactly coordinated, but the sleep is actually (even if Kl. does not know this) brought about by Apollo, and with it the exhaustion joins to the same end.
⟦1⟧ in control of their power. ⟦2⟧ ironic; ⟦3⟧ only here, but Hesych. ⟦4⟧, and ⟦5⟧ ⟦6⟧ (⟦7⟧).

O. Müller introduces meter by placing ⟦1⟧ at the beginning and bringing ⟦2⟧ seven times instead of four; differently Dindorf under the text: A ⟦3⟧. B ⟦4⟧. C ⟦5⟧. The shouts occur as in the hunt (as explained at line 131), to dogs or hunters among themselves ("pay attention").
